_comment: The docs/performance.md §4 git-state matrix, as data rather than as two
setup scripts. Both capture drivers interpret this file, so a state added
here reaches macOS, Linux, and Windows at once — the duplication this
migration exists to delete does not get to reappear in the harness.
Ops: ["git", ...args] runs git in the work tree; ["write", path, text]
and ["mkdir", path] are relative to it; ["remote-track"] creates a bare
remote, adds it as origin and pushes the current branch with -u;
["remote-only"] adds the remote without pushing, leaving no upstream.
_determinism: Commit hashes are rendered output: the detached-HEAD state shows a short
hash, so a fixture is only reproducible if the hash is. Identity, both
dates, the branch name, and the line-ending config are all pinned below,
and every git invocation must carry them or a second run drifts.
The dates are in git's RAW format -- `<unix seconds> <offset>` -- and must
stay that way. An ISO-8601 string here is silently coerced to a [DateTime]
by PowerShell's ConvertFrom-Json and then stringified in the *local*
timezone, so git records the capturing machine's offset in the commit
object. The recorded instant stays right and the hash still changes, which
made the Windows detached-HEAD fixture reproducible only on a machine in
the same timezone as the one that captured it. The raw format is never
mistaken for a date by either driver.

git_states.name: unborn-head
git_states.why: Fresh clone or bare `git init`. porcelain v2 emits `# branch.oid (initial)`, but no `.git/index` exists yet and both scripts guard the whole git block on that file — so every platform renders no git segment here, and it does NOT reach the `(initial)` handling the platforms disagree about. That is `unborn-head-staged`. Keep both: this one pins the guard, that one pins the divergence.

git_states.name: unborn-head-staged
git_states.why: The state that actually reaches `# branch.oid (initial)`: `git add` creates `.git/index`, so the outer guard passes and each script's unborn-HEAD branch is executed. This is the divergence case — bash blanks the branch and renders no git segment, Windows substitutes the literal `HEAD`. Without an index the divergence is unreachable, which is why `unborn-head` alone made the divergence scenario pass vacuously.

git_states.name: clean
git_states.why: The baseline every other state is built from.

git_states.name: untracked-only
git_states.why: Untracked files with no modifications — the count must not be folded into the dirty count.

git_states.name: dirty
git_states.why: A modified tracked file, no untracked files.

git_states.name: stat-dirty
git_states.why: Tracked files rewritten with their own bytes: the index cached stat data no longer matches, but the content does. This is the state that makes `git diff HEAD` refresh and rewrite `.git/index` -- taking `index.lock` in the user repository on every cache miss -- which `--no-optional-locks` does not prevent, because it gates only `cmd_status`. Two files, because one is easy to pass by luck.

git_states.name: stash-present
git_states.why: porcelain v2 emits a `# stash` line only when the count is non-zero.

git_states.name: stash-cleared
git_states.why: The zero case for the state above. `# stash` is omitted entirely rather than reported as 0, which is the shape that broke the parser once already.

git_states.name: ahead-of-upstream
git_states.why: `# branch.ab +1 -0`. Requires a real upstream, so the harness builds a bare remote inside the isolated root.

git_states.name: no-upstream
git_states.why: A remote exists but the branch tracks nothing, so porcelain v2 omits `# branch.ab` altogether.

git_states.name: detached-head
git_states.why: porcelain v2 reports the branch as `(detached)`. A branch literally named `(detached)` is indistinguishable from this — an accepted divergence in §4 — so this case pins what real detached HEAD renders.

git_states.name: collapsed-untracked-dir
git_states.why: porcelain reports an untracked directory as one collapsed `dir/` entry rather than one line per file, so a naive line count under-reports.
